headline: Anthropic and OpenAI employees fear unreleased AI models are too unsafe to release, as SIPRI mapped the military AI industry's influence and Congress moved to tighten chip export controls amid the Nvidia scandal.

points.text: More than two dozen Anthropic and OpenAI employees said internal, unreleased AI models are becoming so powerful that many no longer believe they can be safely released.
SIPRI mapped the actors, influence, and policymaking role of the military artificial intelligence industry.
ChinaTalk examined how a 'Remote Access Rule,' if enforced by Commerce Secretary Lutnick, would buy the US roughly six months of compute lead over China.
Policy Gradients detailed the export control bills most likely to pass tightening AI chip exports during the lame-duck congressional session.

National security and foreign policy experts said Nvidia's centrality to the US economy outweighed concerns about former CEO Jensen Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, as Trump effectively inherited the unresolved scandal by securing his return.
Anthropic built a honeypot test to see whether AI agents would resist temptation to misbehave when given the opportunity to go rogue.
The AI Safety Newsletter reported that Anthropic faces accusations of recklessness as it went public, alongside growing loss-of-control lawsuits against AI companies.
